articles.summary: NEW YORK — JetBlue today announced four vice president appointments across its Legal, Technology and Operations organizations. The appointments include Tim O'Shea as Vice President, Associate General Counsel; Dave MacKinnon as Vice President, Technology Infrastructure and Chief Information Security Officer; and the promotions of Jonathan Wakeman to Vice President, Flight Operations, and Tom Lloyd to Vice President, System Operations. These appointments fill existing leadership positions, with two experienced JetBlue leaders taking on new responsibilities and two executives joining the airline. Dave MacKinnon joins JetBlue as Vice President, Technology Infrastructure and Chief Information Security Officer Dave MacKinnon has joined JetBlue as Vice President, Technology Infrastructure and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), where he will lead the airline's technology infrastructure, cybersecurity and anti-fraud teams. articles.title: JetBlue Announces Vice President Appointments

articles.summary: New “Go Cats Go” aircraft celebrates Broward County's largest airline's expanded partnership with the back-to-back 2024 2025 Stanley Cup champions and underscores commitment to South Florida JetBlue (NASDAQ: JBLU) and the Florida Panthers today unveiled a new special-edition aircraft livery celebrating their expanded partnership and shared South Florida roots. Named “Go Cats Go,” the Airbus A320 brings Panthers colors, logos and team history to the skies while broadly displaying JetBlue’s commitment to Florida. articles.title: JetBlue and the Florida Panthers Take South Florida Dedication to New Heights with New Aircraft Design

articles.summary: Daily flights bring JetBlue to Indianapolis for the first time and mark its return to Columbus, adding to a Fort Lauderdale network that will serve 61 nonstop destinations this winter To celebrate the launch, limited one-way fares are available starting at $59 in Main and $138 in EvenMore only at jetblue.com JetBlue (NASDAQ: JBLU) will launch today daily nonstop flights between Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) and both Indianapolis International Airport (IND) and John Glenn Columbus International Airport (CMH), bringing new travel options to customers in the Midwest as the airline continues to expand its Fort Lauderdale network. The inaugural flights bring JetBlue to Indianapolis for the first time and mark the airline’s return to Columbus. articles.title: JetBlue Launches New Nonstop Service from Fort Lauderdale to Indianapolis and Columbus Today
